message.content:
`docker start` is **not** the command to bring up the Docker Engine itself – it’s used to start *containers* that have already been created.  
On Windows the Docker Engine runs as a Windows Service (or via Docker Desktop). To start the service you can use one of the following:

| Method | Command |
|--------|---------|
| **Command Prompt** | `net start com.docker.service` |
| **PowerShell** | `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service` |
| **Docker Desktop GUI** | Just launch the Docker Desktop application; it will start the service automatically. |

If you’re using Docker Desktop, simply double‑click the Docker icon in your Start menu or system tray. If you prefer the command line, open an elevated (Administrator) PowerShell or CMD window and run the appropriate command above.

> **Tip:**  
> *If you’re trying to start a specific container after the Docker Engine is running, you would then use something like `docker start <container_name_or_id>`.*
